E100.name: Curcumin
E100.explanation: Natural yellow pigment from turmeric. Safe and may have anti-inflammatory benefits.

E102.name: Tartrazine
E102.explanation: Synthetic yellow dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children; banned in some countries.

E110.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
E110.explanation: Synthetic orange-yellow dye. Associated with hyperactivity in children; requires warning label in the EU.

E120.name: Cochineal / Carmine
E120.explanation: Red dye derived from insects. Not suitable for vegans/vegetarians; rare allergic reactions reported.

E129.name: Allura Red AC
E129.explanation: Red synthetic dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children; requires warning in the EU.

E150A.name: Plain Caramel
E150A.explanation: Caramel colouring made by heating sugar alone. Considered safe at food-use levels.

E150D.name: Sulphite Ammonia Caramel
E150D.explanation: Contains 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI), a potential carcinogen. Found in colas and dark sauces.

E160A.name: Beta-Carotene
E160A.explanation: Natural provitamin A colouring. Beneficial antioxidant; safe at food levels.

E160C.name: Paprika Extract
E160C.explanation: Natural red-orange colouring from paprika. No known safety concerns.

E202.name: Potassium Sorbate
E202.explanation: Widely used mould and yeast inhibitor. Regarded as safe by EFSA and FDA.

E211.name: Sodium Benzoate
E211.explanation: Common preservative that can react with vitamin C to form trace benzene, a carcinogen.

E220.name: Sulphur Dioxide
E220.explanation: Preservative in dried fruits and wine. Can trigger asthma and allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

E250.name: Sodium Nitrite
E250.explanation: Used to cure meat and prevent botulism. Linked to increased colorectal cancer risk at high intake.

E251.name: Sodium Nitrate
E251.explanation: Precursor to nitrite in cured meats. Associated with colorectal cancer risk at high dietary exposure.

E290.name: Carbon Dioxide
E290.explanation: Inert gas used for carbonation and packaging. No health concerns at food levels.

E296.name: Malic Acid
E296.explanation: Naturally occurring in fruits. Used as an acidulant; safe at food levels.

E300.name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
E300.explanation: Essential vitamin and antioxidant. Beneficial; found naturally in fruits and vegetables.

E306.name: Mixed Tocopherols
E306.explanation: Natural vitamin E. Antioxidant that helps preserve fats; beneficial at normal food levels.

E320.name: BHA (Butylated Hydroxyanisole)
E320.explanation: Synthetic antioxidant preservative. Classified as possibly carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 2B).

E321.name: BHT (Butylated Hydroxytoluene)
E321.explanation: Synthetic antioxidant. Some studies suggest endocrine disruption; moderation advised.

E322.name: Lecithin
E322.explanation: Natural emulsifier from soy or sunflower. Safe and widely tolerated; soy-derived versions may concern allergy sufferers.

E330.name: Citric Acid
E330.explanation: Found naturally in citrus fruits. Safe for most people; very high amounts may erode tooth enamel.

E331.name: Sodium Citrates
E331.explanation: Sodium salt of citric acid. Used as a buffer and emulsifier; safe at food levels.

E334.name: Tartaric Acid
E334.explanation: Naturally present in grapes and wine. Safe at normal food concentrations.

E338.name: Phosphoric Acid
E338.explanation: Used in colas. High consumption linked to lower bone density due to calcium-phosphorus imbalance.

E340.name: Potassium Phosphates
E340.explanation: Phosphate additive. Excess phosphate intake may impair kidney function; concern at high dietary loads.

E407.name: Carrageenan
E407.explanation: Derived from red seaweed. Some research links degraded forms to gut inflammation; regulatory status under review.

E410.name: Locust Bean Gum
E410.explanation: Natural gum from carob seeds. Safe for most people; may cause bloating in large amounts.

E412.name: Guar Gum
E412.explanation: Natural gum from guar beans. Safe; may lower blood sugar slightly — beneficial for diabetics.

E415.name: Xanthan Gum
E415.explanation: Fermentation-derived thickener. Safe for most people; may cause digestive discomfort in large quantities.

E440.name: Pectin
E440.explanation: Natural fibre-like gelling agent from fruit peel. Safe and may have prebiotic benefits.

E450.name: Diphosphates
E450.explanation: Phosphate salts used as raising agents. Excess phosphate intake may affect kidney function.

E451.name: Triphosphates
E451.explanation: Phosphate raising agent. Same concerns as other phosphates at high dietary loads.

E451I.name: Sodium Triphosphate
E451I.explanation: Phosphate build-up may impair kidney function at high dietary exposure.

E470.name: Fatty Acid Salts
E470.explanation: Salts of fatty acids used as emulsifiers. Generally considered safe at food levels.

E471.name: Mono- and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
E471.explanation: Derived from fats (may include palm or animal fat). Can contain traces of trans fats; moderation advised.

E472E.name: DATEM
E472E.explanation: Diacetyl tartaric acid ester of mono/diglycerides. FDA-approved but associated with heart issues in some animal studies.

E492.name: Sorbitan Tristearate
E492.explanation: Emulsifier used in chocolates and coatings. Considered safe at levels used in food.

E500.name: Sodium Carbonates
E500.explanation: Baking soda family. Common raising agent; safe at food levels.

E500I.name: Sodium Carbonate
E500I.explanation: Used as a raising agent and pH regulator. Safe at normal food concentrations.

E500II.name: Sodium Bicarbonate
E500II.explanation: Baking soda. Safe; contributes to sodium intake if consumed in large quantities.

E501I.name: Potassium Carbonate
E501I.explanation: Stabiliser and raising agent. Safe at food levels.

E503.name: Ammonium Carbonates
E503.explanation: Used in baking; ammonia dissipates during cooking. Safe in finished baked goods.

E508.name: Potassium Chloride
E508.explanation: Salt substitute used to reduce sodium. Excess may affect heart rhythm and kidney function.

E551.name: Silicon Dioxide
E551.explanation: Naturally occurring mineral used to prevent caking in powders. Safe at food levels.

E621.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
E621.explanation: Umami flavour enhancer. Some individuals report sensitivity (headache, flushing) though large studies show no consistent harm.

E627.name: Disodium Guanylate
E627.explanation: Nucleotide flavour enhancer, often paired with MSG. Not suitable for people with gout; may trigger asthma.

E631.name: Disodium Inosinate
E631.explanation: Nucleotide flavour enhancer derived from meat or fish. Not vegan; gout sufferers should avoid.

E635.name: Disodium Ribonucleotides
E635.explanation: Blend of E627 and E631. Potent flavour enhancer; same concerns as its components (gout, asthma).

E950.name: Acesulfame K
E950.explanation: Artificial sweetener ~200x sweeter than sugar. Generally regarded as safe but some studies raise concern about gut microbiome disruption.

E951.name: Aspartame
E951.explanation: Widely used artificial sweetener. IARC classified as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B) in 2023; safe within ADI according to EFSA/FDA. Avoid with PKU.

E952.name: Cyclamate
E952.explanation: Synthetic sweetener banned in the USA; permitted in the EU. Some studies suggest possible carcinogenicity at very high doses.

E955.name: Sucralose
E955.explanation: Made from sugar; 600x sweeter. Generally regarded as safe; some evidence of gut microbiome effects at high doses.

E960.name: Steviol Glycosides (Stevia)
E960.explanation: Natural sweetener from the stevia plant. Safe; may slightly lower blood pressure.
